metadata.name: UDM
metadata.description: Vendor-neutral research administration data model. This JSON is the machine-readable serialization of the specification in vignettes/udm-v2-system-of-record.md: modules, tables, columns in the abstract type vocabulary, constraints, conventions, and derivation rules. It names no database engine; types.dialects maps the abstract types to native ones per engine.

types.description: Column types are the abstract vocabulary. Each dialect entry maps every abstract type to a native type; length, precision, and scale are an adopter's choice and are not normative (the conformance checker compares type families only). scripts/generate_ddl.py resolves a dialect into CREATE TABLE statements. Timestamp is a point in time with its zone preserved; an engine whose mapped type carries no zone (MySQL DATETIME) stores UTC.

identifier.name: Identifier convention
identifier.description: Every table has a primary key named TableName_ID. The primary key is opaque (no business meaning is implied by the value) and unique across the table.

hierarchy.name: Hierarchy
hierarchy.description: Self-referencing parent/child relationships use a Parent_TableName_ID column: an organization's parent unit, an account's parent, an award's prime segment, a cascading subaward's parent, a two-level vocabulary's parent value. A chain to an earlier row of the same table uses Previous_TableName_ID instead: the earlier-stage row (Budget, Effort, CostShare, Payment), the predecessor in a renewal cycle (ComplianceRequirement), the prior version (Document), the proposal-stage role an award-stage role was copied from (TeamRole), or the predecessor in a lineage (Proposal, Award). A hierarchy and a chain are different relationships and carry different names.

role_named_foreign_keys.name: Role-named foreign keys
role_named_foreign_keys.description: A foreign key whose name carries the role of the relationship rather than just the target table. Used on tables that reference the same target table in multiple roles.

polymorphic_attachment.name: Polymorphic attachment
polymorphic_attachment.description: Seven tables in the Attachments domain attach to any listed parent table via Related_Entity_Type + Related_Entity_ID. The Records core module generalizes the everyday RA concept of attaching a document to an award to all the things that accumulate around a record: files, correspondence, restrictions, deadlines, tags, work items, and audit events.

enforcement.description: The seven polymorphic Records tables use a polymorphic foreign key (Related_Entity_Type + Related_Entity_ID) that no single declarative reference can fully enforce.
required_properties: Related_Entity_Type is constrained to a per-attachment allowed list of target table names (enumerated in each attachment's table reference). Optional modules extend a list only through the Records target registry: a module declares which of its tables are attachable, and implementations honor declared targets. A declared target is accepted by every Records attachment table (Document, Communication, Restriction, Deadline, Classification, Action, Approval).
Related_Entity_ID references an existing row in the table named by Related_Entity_Type.
enforcement_options: Database triggers that branch on Related_Entity_Type and verify existence in the matching table.
Application-layer enforcement in every code path that writes to an Attachment table.
Per-target join tables (one bridge table per Attachment x target pair), at the cost of more tables and more join paths.
Scheduled integrity checks that detect and report orphan Attachment rows.
minimum_conformance_behavior: No dangling references on write: INSERT or UPDATE that would set Related_Entity_ID to a non-existent row must be rejected.
Parent removal preserves attachments: a parent row is removed by soft delete (Is_Active = false) rather than hard delete. Attached rows remain in place and retain their FK.

Type-stable references: Related_Entity_Type is not edited after insert. Re-pointing an Attachment at a different parent is done by inserting a new Attachment row, not by mutating an existing one's type.

lifecycle_stage.name: Lifecycle_Stage discriminator
lifecycle_stage.description: Four tables carry a Lifecycle_Stage column that distinguishes records of the same shape at different points in their lifecycle. Later-stage rows store a Previous_*_ID value pointing at the earlier-stage row they descend from. The stage order is canonical; stages may be skipped.
lifecycle_stage.chain_immutability: Once a row at stage S has a later-stage descendant row referencing it through Previous_*_ID, the row at stage S is immutable in the business sense; its primary fields (amount, dates, mode-specific columns) do not change. Corrections after a descendant exists are made by inserting a new row at stage S (with its own descendant chain forward) rather than by editing the existing row. The superseded row is retained for history and is marked Is_Active = false. The Updated_At and audit columns on a frozen row may still be touched (e.g., to record a tombstone or a re-classification of Is_Active); those columns are metadata and not subject to the immutability rule.
lifecycle_stage.no_chain_branching: At any given time, a parent row has at most one descendant via Previous_*_ID with Is_Active = true. If a correction creates a same-stage or later-stage sibling pointing at the same parent, the prior sibling is marked Is_Active = false (superseded). When a same-stage row descends directly from its predecessor (a correction, or an Effort recertification), the predecessor is marked Is_Active = false; the per-stage non-overlap rules apply to active rows, so the superseded row no longer counts. This makes 'the latest leaf' unambiguous: it is the unique active descendant chain ending at a row with no active descendant. Multiple concurrent active siblings are a data error.

two_fk_exclusive_or.name: Two-FK exclusive-or attachment
two_fk_exclusive_or.description: Some tables attach to one of two possible parents via two nullable foreign key columns and a constraint that exactly one is non-null. The pattern keeps Award and Subaward symmetrical without requiring duplicate satellite tables.

allowed_values.name: Extensibility via AllowedValues
allowed_values.description: The AllowedValues table holds institution-specific enumerated values. Optional modules may define their own Value_Groups (a sanctioned extension point). Tables that reference institution-defined enums use a *_Value_ID foreign key. Tables that need universal enumerations use a fixed value list enforced by the database's enumeration mechanism.
allowed_values.decision_rule: A field is a fixed Status enum when (a) the value set is standardized across institutions AND (b) the model's correctness depends on stable, known values. A field is an AllowedValues FK when (a) institutions need to add or retire local values, OR (b) no canonical interop list exists, OR (c) the field is local classification not consulted by the model's constraints.

boolean_naming.name: Boolean naming
boolean_naming.description: Boolean columns are prefixed Is_ (e.g. Is_Active, Is_Flow_Through, Is_Key_Personnel).

audit_columns.description: Every table, in core and optional modules alike, includes these columns. They are not repeated in the per-table reference; assume them present everywhere unless explicitly overridden.

Source_System.description: The originating source system (ERP financial system, eRA platform, HR system, etc.)

Source_Record_ID.description: The originating record's identifier in the source system; preserves provenance for downstream reconciliation

Is_Active.description: Default true; used for soft-delete and to distinguish currently-valid records from historical ones. Tables with their own lifecycle/status fields may rely on those instead and treat Is_Active as always true

audit_authority.description: Two mechanisms touch the question 'when did this change?' and each answers a different scope.

mechanisms.Updated_At: Marks the moment of the most recent write to the row. Single timestamp, overwritten on every update; preserves no history. Answers: is this row stale.
mechanisms.Versioned storage: Dolt, Trino on Apache Iceberg, temporal tables in Postgres / SQL Server — the storage layer captures full row history with transaction metadata (actor, timestamp). Time-travel queries reconstruct any field's prior value at any past point in time without application instrumentation. Answers: what did column X look like on date D, and which business events touched this row.

audit_authority.conflict_resolution: Updated_At marks the latest write; any history question deeper than that resolves at the storage layer. The 'Audit record shape' pattern (vignettes/udm-v2-patterns.md) documents the canonical projected shape.

conventions.is_active_vs_status: Tables that carry their own primary lifecycle/status field (Award_Status, Subaward_Status, Requirement_Status, Action_Status, Restriction_Status, Deadline_Status, Payment_Status, Negotiation_Status, RFA_Status) treat that status field as authoritative for what state this record is in, and use Is_Active only to hide rows from operational queries (without losing them). A row may be Is_Active = false while its status field still records a meaningful state. When the two conflict, operational consumers use Is_Active; auditors use the status field.

constraint_vocabulary.description: Structured constraint types used in the structured field of a table's constraints. Code generators may consume these to emit CHECK constraints, triggers, deferrable constraints, or scheduled integrity checks. A structured entry with for_every = "date D" holds for every date D: its active_filter is evaluated with D bound to each date, so the rule governs history, not only today.

types.xor: Exactly one of the listed columns must be non-null, unconditionally. Stage-conditional exclusive-or rules (Budget, CostShare: exactly one of Award_ID/Subaward_ID non-null only at or beyond a given Lifecycle_Stage) are NOT declared with column-level xor_with; they are expressed as conditional_required on the columns and a constraint on the table.
types.at_least_one_of: At least one of the listed columns must be non-null.
types.at_most_one_of: At most one of the listed columns may be non-null.
types.conditional_required: A column is required when a predicate over other columns holds.
types.unique_scope: A column or column tuple is unique within a scope (whole table or a row partition defined by other columns). With an optional condition, only rows satisfying the condition are unique within the columns (a partial unique index).
types.non_overlap_ranges: For rows in a partition, (Start_Date, End_Date) ranges are non-overlapping. Null End_Date treated as +infinity.
types.aggregate_equality: An aggregate over a partition equals a value derived from another row.
types.no_gap_periods: For consecutive rows in a partition (ordered by Period_Start_Date), the next row's Period_Start_Date equals the prior row's Period_End_Date + 1 day.
types.mutual_exclusion_by_canonical_role: Rows resolving to one canonical role cannot coexist with active rows resolving to another canonical role within the same partition.
types.at_most_one_true_in_partition: Within a partition, at most one row has the named boolean column = true.
types.referenced_has_capability: A foreign key target row has an OrganizationCapability with a specified canonical capability.
types.referenced_status_is: A foreign key target row has a specific value in a named status column.

value_normalization.description: For vendor-neutral cross-institution queries to work, Value_Group names in AllowedValues are canonical. Individual institutions populate their own Value_Code rows.
recommendations: A Canonical_Value_Code column on AllowedValues that institutions populate with the canonical code their local Value_Code maps to.
Queries that aggregate across institutions group by Canonical_Value_Code rather than Value_Code.
semantic_contract: A *_Value_ID column resolves to canonical code X when the AllowedValues row it references has Canonical_Value_Code = X, or Value_Code = X when Canonical_Value_Code is null. Every constraint, convention, and derivation rule that says "resolves to" means this.
A null Canonical_Value_Code means the local code has no canonical equivalent. Cross-institution queries that group on Canonical_Value_Code exclude such rows.
A Value_Code marked Is_Active = false is retired. Existing rows that reference a retired code retain their FK.

The spec ships canonical codes for values that load-bearing constraints depend on (the recommended_values on each vocabulary column, plus any canonical codes named in a table's constraints). Adopters extend the canonical set for additional analytics dimensions through external coordination such as a consortium or working group.

lifecycle_closure.description: What happens to a parent's children when its status becomes Closed or Terminated. Work and obligations survive closure, because closeout is what generates them; coverage and sub-agreements do not, because they describe what is active. The institution chooses the mechanism (trigger, scheduled job, application workflow); the schema records the resulting state.

rules.when: Award_Status or Subaward_Status becomes Closed or Terminated
rules.then: Open TeamRole rows on the agreement (End_Date null) are end-dated on the date of the status change.

rules.when: Award_Status or Subaward_Status becomes Closed or Terminated
rules.then: Active Restrictions on the agreement become Expired when they lapse by date or Lifted when removed by decision; a closed agreement carries no Active restriction.

rules.when: Award_Status or Subaward_Status becomes Closed or Terminated
rules.then: Open ComplianceCoverage rows for the agreement (Coverage_End_Date null) are end-dated on the date of the status change.
Every Subaward whose Prime_Award_ID is the Award is already Closed or Terminated. The prime closes last; this is a constraint on Award.
Every Subaward whose Prime_Award_ID is the Award and whose Subaward_Status is Active or Suspended becomes Terminated on the same date.

rules.when: Award_Status or Subaward_Status becomes Closed or Terminated

lifecycle_closure.default: A child not named here is unchanged by its parent's status change.

semantic.name: Lifecycle_Stage vs *_Status
semantic.criterion: Whether the row's shape changes between states.
semantic.lifecycle_stage_use: Used when different stages require different columns to be populated (Budget at Modular vs Approved-with-period, Effort at Charged adds Charged_Amount, Effort at Certified adds Statement/Signature, Payment at Invoiced adds Invoice_Number). The Previous_*_ID chain plus chain immutability is justified by the row's shape changing as the stage advances.
semantic.bare_status_use: Used when the row carries the same columns at every state (Award_Status, Subaward_Status, Requirement_Status, Report_Status, Modification.Approval_Status). No chain immutability is required because corrections at a status point don't conflict with later rows of different shape.

semantic.name: TeamRole vs OrganizationRole vs ProtocolRole
semantic.description: Three parallel person-in-role tables, each answering a different question.

tables.TeamRole: Who is on the team performing this Award (PI, Co_I, Coordinator, etc., with effort and credit allocation).
tables.OrganizationRole: Who holds a role at this Organization (committee member, program officer at the sponsor, Authorized Official at the subrecipient, financial contact at the vendor, institutional Sponsored Programs liaison). Optionally scoped to an Award, Subaward, or RFA.
tables.ProtocolRole: Who is on the team for this compliance protocol (Primary_Investigator, Co_Investigator, study coordinator, lab manager, TCP-cleared personnel).

cross_table_examples: An external Co-Investigator at a subrecipient institution is recorded as BOTH an TeamRole row (their scientific role on the Award/Subaward, with credit allocation) AND an OrganizationRole row scoped to the Subaward (their administrative role at the subrecipient organization for that subaward).
A person who is the responsible PI on an IRB protocol covering an Award has both an TeamRole row (PI on the Award) and a ProtocolRole row (Primary_Investigator on the protocol).

modules.description: Everything specified is a module: a named, fully specified, versioned slice of research administration capability. Core modules are required of every implementation; optional modules are adopted by declaration; local extensions are institution-specific and unspecified; implementation tables are spec machinery outside the capability taxonomy. Every module, core or optional, follows every core convention: the identifier convention, the universal audit columns, boolean naming, and the abstract type vocabulary.

laws.capability_criterion: Every module, core or optional, must be a capability an institution recognizably exercises: the adopter can finish the sentence 'we do X.' Universality decides the tier: a capability every research institution exercises is a core module; a capability only some institutions exercise is an optional module. Modules are carved by story, never by abstraction depth.
laws.encapsulation_rule: A module may add its own tables, which may reference core tables (and declared module dependencies) by foreign key, and nothing else. It may not add columns to, alter constraints of, or extend the closed vocabularies of the core or of other modules. Two sanctioned extension points exist by design: (1) the Records target registry: a module declares which of its tables are attachable, and the core Records tables honor declared targets; (2) AllowedValues: a module may define its own value groups. Anything a module needs beyond that is either a core change (shipped in a core minor release, justified on its own merits, harmless without the module) with the module declaring a minimum core version, or it isn't core's business.

example_views.name: vw_All_ContactDetails
example_views.purpose: Unified contact details from both Personnel and Organization owners, with the owner type and name surfaced so consumers can query 'all email addresses on file' or 'all contacts for organization X' without unioning the two XOR cases manually.
example_views.sql:
CREATE VIEW vw_All_ContactDetails AS
SELECT
  cd.ContactDetails_ID,
  CASE WHEN cd.Personnel_ID IS NOT NULL THEN 'Personnel' ELSE 'Organization' END AS Owner_Type,
  COALESCE(cd.Personnel_ID, cd.Organization_ID) AS Owner_ID,
  CASE WHEN cd.Personnel_ID IS NOT NULL THEN CONCAT(p.First_Name, ' ', p.Last_Name) ELSE o.Organization_Name END AS Owner_Name,
  ct.Value_Code AS Contact_Type_Code,
  cd.Contact_Value,
  cd.Is_Primary
FROM ContactDetails cd
LEFT JOIN Personnel p ON cd.Personnel_ID = p.Personnel_ID
LEFT JOIN Organization o ON cd.Organization_ID = o.Organization_ID
JOIN AllowedValues ct ON cd.Contact_Type_Value_ID = ct.AllowedValue_ID
WHERE cd.Is_Active = true;

In_Review.set_by: Derived from the Approval rows of the current round

Returned.definition: An approval step sent it back for revision; it must be rerouted
Returned.set_by: Derived from the Approval rows of the current round

Approved.definition: Every approval step has approved; the proposal may be submitted
Approved.set_by: Derived from the Approval rows of the current round

Rejected.definition: An approval step refused it; the proposal does not proceed
Rejected.set_by: Derived from the Approval rows of the current round

Internal_Approval_Status.description: Where the proposal stands in the institution's internal approval chain. Draft until routed; In_Review while steps are pending; Returned when a step sent it back for revision; Approved once every step has approved; Rejected when a step refused it. A proposal is submitted only once this is Approved

derived.rule: Draft when no Approval row exists for the Proposal; otherwise, over the rows of the highest Approval_Round: Rejected if any row is Rejected; Returned if any row is Returned_for_Revision; Approved if every row is Approved or Bypassed; In_Review otherwise.
derived.recompute_triggers: On insert/update of any Approval row whose Related_Entity_Type is Proposal and Related_Entity_ID is the Proposal.

Unapproved.definition: The internal approval chain has not reached Approved, so nothing can be sent

Unsent.definition: Approved internally; no transmission attempted yet

Submitting.definition: The newest attempt is in transmission

Received.definition: The sponsor's system acknowledged the newest attempt

Validated.definition: The sponsor's system passed its checks on the newest attempt

Invalid.definition: The sponsor's system rejected the newest attempt on its checks; a new attempt is needed

Accepted.definition: The sponsor took the newest attempt for review; the decision stage begins

Failed.definition: The newest attempt did not complete transmission; a new attempt is needed

Withdrawn.definition: The institution pulled the newest attempt back; the decision stage returns to Unsubmitted

Submission_Status.description: Where the proposal stands with the sponsor's submission system. Unapproved until the internal approval chain reaches Approved; Unsent once approved and before the first attempt; then the newest SubmissionAttempt's Attempt_Status. Derived

derived.rule: Unapproved while Internal_Approval_Status is not Approved; Unsent when Approved and no SubmissionAttempt exists; otherwise the Attempt_Status of the SubmissionAttempt with the highest Attempt_Number.
derived.recompute_triggers: On insert/update of Proposal.Internal_Approval_Status; on insert/update of any SubmissionAttempt for the Proposal.

Unsubmitted.definition: No attempt has been accepted by the sponsor, or the newest attempt was withdrawn

Pending.definition: The sponsor holds the proposal and has not decided

Intent_to_Award.definition: The sponsor signalled funding before an agreement exists; at-risk spending may be authorized

Awarded.definition: The sponsor funded it; an Award row exists

Declined.definition: The sponsor did not fund it

Decision_Status.description: The sponsor's disposition of the proposal. Unsubmitted until an attempt is Accepted (and while the newest attempt is Withdrawn); Pending once the sponsor holds it; Intent_to_Award when the sponsor signals funding before an agreement; Awarded or Declined on the decision. Unsubmitted and Pending follow the submission stage; the rest are set from the sponsor's communication

Decision_Date.description: When the sponsor's disposition was received: the Intent_to_Award, Awarded, or Declined date

Low.definition: Low risk; routine review and monitoring

Medium.definition: Moderate risk; heightened review and monitoring

High.definition: High risk; closest review and monitoring

Risk_Level.description: Institutional risk rating for the proposal, used to set review intensity

Proposal_Type_Value_ID.description: The kind of proposal relative to prior submissions

Mechanism_Value_ID.description: The sponsor's funding mechanism applied for
Mechanism_Value_ID.synonyms: Funding Mechanism, Activity Code, Award Type

constraints.rule: Decision_Status is Unsubmitted while no SubmissionAttempt for the Proposal has Attempt_Status Accepted, or while the newest attempt is Withdrawn; otherwise it is Pending, Intent_to_Award, Awarded, or Declined.
Decision_Status = 'Awarded' only when Internal_Approval_Status = 'Approved'.
The Previous_Proposal_ID chain is acyclic: following it from any row reaches a row whose Previous_Proposal_ID is null.

SubmissionAttempt.description: One transmission of a proposal to a sponsor's submission system. The newest attempt's Attempt_Status is the proposal's Submission_Status. The attempt records what was sent, by whom, when, and what the sponsor's system said; package assembly, connection profiles, and retry mechanics stay in the System of Engagement.

Attempt_Number.description: 1 for the first attempt; consecutive within the Proposal

Channel_Value_ID.description: How the proposal went to the sponsor

Submitted_By_Personnel_ID.description: Who transmitted the attempt: the authorized organizational representative, or the person they released it to

Submitted_At.conditional_required: Required when Attempt_Status is Submitted, Received, Validated, Invalid, or Accepted
Submitted_At.description: When the transmission was sent. Required once Attempt_Status is Submitted or later

Validated.definition: The sponsor's system passed its checks

Invalid.definition: The sponsor's system rejected it on its checks; terminal for this attempt

Accepted.definition: The sponsor took it for review; terminal for this attempt

Failed.definition: Transmission did not complete; terminal for this attempt

Withdrawn.definition: The institution pulled it back; terminal for this attempt

Attempt_Status.description: The attempt's state as the sponsor's system reports it. Unsent while assembled but not transmitted; Submitting during transmission; Submitted once sent; Received when the sponsor's system acknowledged it; Validated or Invalid on the sponsor's checks; Accepted when the sponsor took it for review; Failed when transmission did not complete; Withdrawn when the institution pulled it back
Attempt_Status.synonyms: Submission Status, Grants.gov Status, Portal Status

Tracking_Identifier.description: The identifier the sponsor's system assigned to this transmission
Tracking_Identifier.synonyms: Tracking Number, Confirmation Number, Grants.gov Tracking ID

Sponsor_Acknowledged_At.description: When the sponsor's system acknowledged receipt

Package_Hash.description: SHA-256 of the assembled package as transmitted, so a sign-off can be matched to what went out

Notes.description: Free text: validation messages, the reason for a withdrawal

constraints.rule: Attempt_Number is unique within the Proposal and consecutive from 1.
Submitted_At is required when Attempt_Status is Submitted, Received, Validated, Invalid, or Accepted.
At most one SubmissionAttempt per Proposal has Attempt_Status Unsent or Submitting: one attempt is in flight at a time.
SubmissionAttempt rows exist only for a Proposal whose Internal_Approval_Status is Approved.

PreAwardAuthorization.description: An institutional pre-award authorization to spend at-risk on a Proposal that has been favorably reviewed but not yet officially awarded.

Authorizing_Personnel_ID.description: The institutional officer who authorized the at-risk spending

Expired_Unused.definition: The window closed without an award and without conversion

Authorization_Status.description: Constrained: Pending / Approved / Revoked / Converted_To_Award / Expired_Unused

Converted_To_Award_ID.description: Required when Authorization_Status = 'Converted_To_Award'; otherwise null. Populated once the Proposal becomes an Award and the pre-award authorization is folded into the executed funding

constraints.rule: The Proposal referenced by Proposal_ID has Decision_Status Pending or Intent_to_Award.

Funding_Mechanism_Description.description: Free-text description for mechanisms not in the canonical taxonomy

Original_Start_Date.description: Start of the originally authorized Period of Performance at award execution. Frozen; not adjusted by Modifications.

Original_End_Date.description: End of the originally authorized Period of Performance at award execution. Frozen. To query the live end date after extensions, use Current_End_Date.

Current_End_Date.description: Current end after Modifications. Derived from Modifications.

Original_Total_Funded.description: Funded amount at award execution. Frozen.

derived.rule: The Award's Original_Total_Funded plus the sum of Funding_Change_Amount across Modifications where Award_ID = the Award, Approval_Status = 'Approved', and Is_Active = true. Modifications with null Funding_Change_Amount (non-financial event types) contribute 0.
derived.recompute_triggers: On insert/update of any Modification on the Award, including a change to its Is_Active; on insert/update of Award.

Current_PI_Personnel_ID.description: The current PI when in single-PI mode; null when in Multi_PI mode or when no PI is active. Query-convenience denormalization parallel to Current_End_Date and Current_Total_Funded. TeamRole remains canonical for full team membership.

derived.rule: The Personnel_ID of the unique active TeamRole row on this Award where Role_Value_ID resolves to canonical 'PI' and the row is active on today's date (Start_Date <= today AND (End_Date IS NULL OR End_Date >= today)). Null when no such row exists — either the Award is in Multi_PI mode or no PI/Multi_PI rows are active (community-partner Subaward case). derived.recompute_triggers: On insert/update of any TeamRole row on this Award; on the daily rollover that may change which rows are active on today's date.

conventions.name: Modification vs Parent_Award_ID vs Previous_Award_ID
conventions.discriminator: Whether the sponsor issues a new Award_Number
rules: If the sponsor action does NOT issue a new Award_Number, it is a Modification on the existing Award (NCE, administrative supplement, budget revision, scope change, PI change, rebudget).
If the sponsor action issues a new Award_Number that is part of an incremental segment under the same prime, it is a new Award with Parent_Award_ID set to the predecessor.

If the sponsor action issues a new Award_Number through a competing renewal that supersedes a prior award identity, it is a new Award with Previous_Award_ID set to the predecessor (parallel to Proposal.Previous_Proposal_ID).
conventions.subaward_rule: Modification vs new Subaward with Parent_Subaward_ID (cascading or amended subawards under the same prime). Subaward competing-renewal lineage flows through the Prime Award chain — when the prime renews to a new Award, a new Subaward at the same subrecipient is created under the new Prime; the predecessor Subaward is end-dated on the old Prime. No Previous_Subaward_ID column is needed.

conventions.name: Group_ID and Originating_Proposal_ID
conventions.description: Two independent mechanisms answer what group does this Award or Proposal belong to.

mechanisms.Originating_Proposal_ID: Derived root of the Previous_Proposal_ID lineage chain. Auto-updates if the lineage is corrected.
mechanisms.Group_ID: User-maintained grouping label. The institution sets it deliberately and lineage edits do not change it.

conventions.agreement_or_disagreement: These can agree or disagree, and the disagreement is informative: lineage may continue while the institution chooses to fork the Group identity (or vice versa).
prefill_rules: On Award insert, Award.Group_ID is pre-filled from the originating Proposal's Group_ID as a default; may be overridden afterward.
On Subaward insert, Subaward.Group_ID is pre-filled from the Prime Award's Group_ID when a Prime exists, otherwise from the originating Proposal's Group_ID.

conventions.name: Lineage mechanisms overview
conventions.description: Twelve lineage-adjacent columns exist across Proposal (3), Award (5), and Subaward (4). Pick the column that matches the query.

query_to_column_map.question: What proposal originated this planned Subaward?
What is the Prime Award for this Subaward?
What is this Proposal a resubmission / renewal of?
What is the root Proposal of a renewal chain?
What is this Award a competing renewal of?
What is the root Award of a renewal chain?
What other Awards are incremental segments under the same prime?
What is the predecessor Subaward in a renewal?
query_to_column_map.use: walk Subaward.Prime_Award_ID -> Award.Previous_Award_ID, then find Subaward with matching Subrecipient_Organization_ID. No dedicated Previous_Subaward_ID column.

query_to_column_map.question: What other Subawards cascade or were amended under the same prime?
What institutional research-line group does this belong to?

conventions.originating_id_semantics: Originating_Proposal_ID and Originating_Award_ID are derived stored columns that point at the root of the Previous_*_ID chain. They are null when the row is itself the root (Previous_*_ID is null). Queries for 'all rows in this lineage chain' use COALESCE(Originating_*_ID, *_ID) to handle both cases uniformly. Example: SELECT * FROM Award WHERE COALESCE(Originating_Award_ID, Award_ID) = COALESCE(:x_originating, :x_award_id);

conventions.name: Just-In-Time (JIT) cycle
conventions.description: Sponsor JIT requests arrive between Proposal submission and Award. The exchange is captured by composition rather than by a dedicated entity.
composition: The sponsor's request is an Action row with Action_Type resolving to JIT_Request, attached to the Proposal. The Action's Outcome_Description records the resolution; Linked_Document_ID points at the formal JIT response when filed.
The sponsor's correspondence transmitting the request and the institution's reply are Communication rows attached to the same Proposal.
Updated Other Support is an OtherSupportDisclosure row with Disclosure_Type = 'JIT' and Triggering_Proposal_ID set to the Proposal.
An updated budget at JIT follows the Budget Proposed-stage revisions rule.

JIT-driven compliance approvals (an IRB approval letter the sponsor wants before issuing the NoA, an export-control determination, etc.) are recorded as a ComplianceRequirement row of the appropriate Requirement_Type with Submitted_Date and Approved_Date populated. The approval document attaches to the ComplianceRequirement as a Document. The JIT_Request Action's Linked_Document_ID may also point at the same document.

conventions.name: Sponsor decision artifacts (NoA, decline letter, modification notice)
conventions.description: Sponsor-issued decision documents have three independent representations.
representations: The document itself (the NoA PDF, the modification notice email) is a Document row with the appropriate Document_Type attached to the relevant entity (Proposal, Award, Modification).

The decision's effect on schema state is captured by updating the relevant status field (Proposal.Decision_Status='Awarded', Modification.Approval_Status='Approved') with the transition preserved by the storage layer's versioned history.
The accompanying correspondence (program officer's email transmitting the decision) is a Communication row attached to the same parent.
conventions.note: No single entity captures 'the decision' abstractly; the three representations together do.

conventions.name: Internal funding represented as an Award
conventions.description: An internally-funded pilot is modeled as an Award row whose Sponsor_Organization_ID is the internal sponsor (the VPR's office, the dean's office, etc.). Budget, Transaction, Payment, CostShare, Equipment, FinanceCode, Modification, and Closeout all attach to that Award using the same structures as for an externally-funded Award. The funding instrument is always an Award (or Subaward) regardless of whether the sponsor is external or internal.

conventions.name: Submission attempts
conventions.description: The fact that a proposal went to a sponsor is research administration data; the mechanics of assembling and transmitting it are not.
rules: Each transmission is one SubmissionAttempt row. Re-submissions add attempts; the attempt history is the row sequence by Attempt_Number.
Proposal.Submission_Status is the newest attempt's Attempt_Status; Proposal.Submission_Date and Submission_Version derive from the attempts.
Sponsor tracking and confirmation identifiers live on the attempt, indexed, not in free text.

Package assembly artifacts, connection profiles, and retry mechanics are submission-tooling internals and live in the System of Engagement. The transmitted package itself is a Document attached to the attempt; its hash is Package_Hash.
A later minor release may add the sponsor's system as a named channel value; the Channel vocabulary is institution-extensible.

example_views.name: vw_Active_Awards
example_views.purpose: Currently-active Awards with derived current-state columns and the operating Sponsor.
example_views.sql:
CREATE VIEW vw_Active_Awards AS
SELECT
  a.Award_ID,
  a.Award_Number,
  a.FAIN,
  a.Award_Title,
  a.Award_Status,
  a.Sponsor_Organization_ID,
  a.Administering_Organization_ID,
  a.Mechanism_Value_ID,
  a.Group_ID,
  a.Original_Start_Date,
  a.Original_End_Date,
  a.Current_End_Date,
  a.Original_Total_Funded,
  a.Current_Total_Funded,
  a.Current_PI_Personnel_ID
FROM Award a
WHERE a.Award_Status = 'Active'
  AND a.Is_Active = true;

example_views.name: vw_Award_Lineage
example_views.purpose: Computes the lineage root for every active Award via COALESCE(Originating_Award_ID, Award_ID). Consumers query 'all Awards in a research line' by selecting where Lineage_Root_Award_ID equals the same expression for the target Award.
example_views.sql:
CREATE VIEW vw_Award_Lineage AS
SELECT
  a.Award_ID,
  a.Award_Number,
  COALESCE(a.Originating_Award_ID, a.Award_ID) AS Lineage_Root_Award_ID,
  a.Group_ID,
  a.Award_Status,
  a.Parent_Award_ID
FROM Award a
WHERE a.Is_Active = true;
example_views.usage_example: SELECT * FROM vw_Award_Lineage WHERE Lineage_Root_Award_ID = (SELECT COALESCE(Originating_Award_ID, Award_ID) FROM Award WHERE Award_ID = :target_award_id);

example_views.name: vw_Subaward_With_Prime
example_views.purpose: Subaward joined with its Prime Award (when one exists). Pre-award Subawards (Subaward_Status = 'Proposed') return NULL on the Prime side.
example_views.sql:
CREATE VIEW vw_Subaward_With_Prime AS
SELECT
  s.Subaward_ID,
  s.Subaward_Number,
  s.Subaward_Status,
  s.Subrecipient_Organization_ID,
  s.Total_Subaward_Amount,
  s.Original_Start_Date AS Sub_Start_Date,
  s.Current_End_Date AS Sub_Current_End_Date,
  s.Current_PI_Personnel_ID AS Sub_Current_PI_Personnel_ID,
  p.Award_ID AS Prime_Award_ID,
  p.Award_Number AS Prime_Award_Number,
  p.FAIN AS Prime_FAIN,
  p.Award_Status AS Prime_Award_Status,
  p.Sponsor_Organization_ID AS Prime_Sponsor_Organization_ID
FROM Subaward s
LEFT JOIN Award p ON s.Prime_Award_ID = p.Award_ID
WHERE s.Is_Active = true;

example_views.name: vw_Overdue_Reports
example_views.purpose: Reports whose Due_Date is in the past and whose Report_Status indicates they have not been accepted or waived.
example_views.sql:
CREATE VIEW vw_Overdue_Reports AS
SELECT
  r.Report_ID,
  r.Award_ID,
  r.Subaward_ID,
  r.Report_Type,
  r.Reporting_Period_Start_Date,
  r.Reporting_Period_End_Date,
  r.Due_Date,
  r.Report_Status,
  DATEDIFF(CURRENT_DATE, r.Due_Date) AS Days_Overdue
FROM Report r
WHERE r.Due_Date < CURRENT_DATE
  AND r.Report_Status IN ('Pending', 'Drafted', 'Returned_for_Revision', 'Late')
  AND r.Is_Active = true;

example_views.name: vw_Award_Budget_Summary
example_views.purpose: Original vs Current funding and end-date for each Award, showing the net effect of approved Modifications.
example_views.sql:
CREATE VIEW vw_Award_Budget_Summary AS
SELECT
  a.Award_ID,
  a.Award_Number,
  a.Original_Total_Funded,
  a.Current_Total_Funded,
  (a.Current_Total_Funded - a.Original_Total_Funded) AS Net_Modification_Amount,
  a.Original_End_Date,
  a.Current_End_Date,
  DATEDIFF(a.Current_End_Date, a.Original_End_Date) AS Days_Extended
FROM Award a
WHERE a.Is_Active = true;

example_views.name: vw_Approved_Modifications
example_views.purpose: Approved Modifications with the Event_Type resolved to its canonical code and the financial / date impact surfaced. Excludes Reversed Modifications.
example_views.sql:
CREATE VIEW vw_Approved_Modifications AS
SELECT
  m.Modification_ID,
  m.Award_ID,
  m.Subaward_ID,
  m.Modification_Number,
  m.Effective_Date,
  av.Value_Code AS Event_Type_Code,
  av.Canonical_Value_Code AS Canonical_Event_Type,
  m.Funding_Change_Amount,
  m.New_End_Date,
  m.Approval_Status,
  m.Description
FROM Modification m
JOIN AllowedValues av ON m.Event_Type_Value_ID = av.AllowedValue_ID
WHERE m.Approval_Status = 'Approved'
  AND m.Is_Active = true;

effort.name: Effort
effort.story: We commit and certify effort on funded work

TeamRole.description: A person's role on a proposal and, once funded, on the award or subaward, with effort allocation, date range, and credit attribution. Anchored like Budget: Proposal_ID is always set; Award_ID or Subaward_ID is set once the proposal is funded. On award creation the proposal-stage rows are copied as new rows that carry the agreement and point back through Previous_TeamRole_ID; the proposal-stage rows remain as the record of the proposed team. Limited to team staffing roles.
TeamRole.authoritative_source_note: TeamRole.FTE_Percent is the authoritative committed-effort figure for an Award. The Effort table carries per-period, per-stage detail and is authoritative for actual effort questions (Charged, Certified).

TeamRole_ID.synonyms: Project Role ID, Investigator Assignment, Personnel Assignment

Proposal_ID.description: The proposal the role was proposed on. Always set; stable across the proposal-stage row and the award-stage rows copied from it

Award_ID.description: The Award the role is on once the proposal is funded. At most one of Award_ID or Subaward_ID is non-null; both null while the row is proposal-stage

Subaward_ID.description: The Subaward the role is on once the proposal is funded. At most one of Award_ID or Subaward_ID is non-null; both null while the row is proposal-stage

Previous_TeamRole_ID.description: Chain pointer. An award-stage row points at the proposal-stage row it was copied from; null on proposal-stage rows and on roles added after funding

Role_Value_ID.description: The person's role on the agreement
Role_Value_ID.synonyms: Role, Position, Investigator Role, Personnel Role

FTE_Percent.description: Committed effort percentage (0.00-100.00). On a proposal-stage row the proposed commitment; on an award-stage row the committed one. Authoritative 'what was promised' figure. Institutions typically arrange a person's concurrent FTE commitments not to exceed 100%, but this is a data invariant; spec does not enforce a per-person sum.
FTE_Percent.synonyms: Effort Percentage, Committed Effort, Time Allocation

Credit_Percent.description: Investigator credit allocation. Institutions typically arrange Credit_Percent to sum to 100 across active credit-bearing roles on the parent agreement, but spec does not enforce a sum-to-100 constraint.
Credit_Percent.synonyms: Credit Allocation, Investigator Credit, Research Credit

Is_Key_Personnel.description: Whether the person is designated key/senior personnel

Is_Contact_PI.conditional_required: Required (defaulting to false) when Role_Value_ID resolves to canonical Multi_PI; null otherwise.
Is_Contact_PI.description: Identifies the NIH MPI Contact PI on a multi-PI Award. At most one active Multi_PI row per parent agreement has Is_Contact_PI = true.
Is_Contact_PI.synonyms: Contact PI, Lead Multi-PI, MPI Lead, NIH Contact PI

Start_Date.description: When the person assumed the role

End_Date.description: When the person left the role; null while current

constraints.rule: At most one of Award_ID or Subaward_ID is non-null; both are null while the row is proposal-stage.
When Award_ID is set, Award.Proposal_ID equals this row's Proposal_ID; when Subaward_ID is set, Subaward.Proposal_ID equals it. A role moves to the agreement its proposal became.
Previous_TeamRole_ID, when set, references a row with the same Proposal_ID whose Award_ID and Subaward_ID are both null: an award-stage row descends from a proposal-stage row.
For a given (proposal or agreement, Personnel_ID, Role_Value_ID), the (Start_Date, End_Date) ranges are non-overlapping (null End_Date is treated as +infinity).
FTE_Percent is between 0.00 and 100.00.

PI vs Multi_PI mode is exclusive. For a given proposal or agreement at any active date, either exactly one active TeamRole row has Role_Value_ID resolving to canonical PI (single-PI mode), or two-or-more active rows have Role_Value_ID resolving to canonical Multi_PI (multi-PI mode), or zero of either (community-partner Subaward). An Award or Subaward cannot simultaneously have an active PI row and active Multi_PI rows.

structured.active_filter: Is_Active = true AND Start_Date <= D AND (End_Date IS NULL OR End_Date >= D)

constraints.rule: At most one Contact PI per Multi_PI agreement. For a given proposal or agreement in Multi_PI mode and any date D, at most one row covering D has Is_Contact_PI = true.

structured.active_filter: Is_Active = true AND Role_Value_ID resolves to Multi_PI AND Start_Date <= D AND (End_Date IS NULL OR End_Date >= D)

Effort.description: Per-stage effort detail for an TeamRole. The Lifecycle_Stage column distinguishes proposed, approved, charged, and certified effort numbers.

TeamRole_ID.description: References TeamRole (the assignment). Proposed-stage Effort references the proposal-stage row; Approved and later stages reference the award-stage row

Approved.definition: Effort committed in the award as funded

Charged.definition: Salary actually charged for the period

Certified.definition: Effort attested after the fact by the certifier; carries the statement they accepted

Previous_Effort_ID.description: Chain pointer. Later-stage rows point at nearest existing earlier-stage row. Same-stage recertification (Certified -> Certified) also chains via this column.

Period_Start_Date.description: Start of the effort reporting period

Period_End_Date.description: End of the effort reporting period

Effort_Percent.synonyms: Time Spent, Period Effort, Charged Effort

Person_Months.description: Person-months of effort in the period: Effort_Percent / 100 times the months in the Calendar_Type (12 Calendar, 9 Academic, 3 Summer). Stored because sponsors report effort in person-months

derived.rule: Effort_Percent / 100 multiplied by 12 when Calendar_Type = 'Calendar', by 9 when 'Academic', by 3 when 'Summer'.
derived.recompute_triggers: On insert/update of Effort.Effort_Percent or Effort.Calendar_Type.

Calendar_Type.synonyms: Effort Calendar, Appointment Type, Calendar Basis

Over_Cap_Amount.conditional_required: Required when Lifecycle_Stage = 'Charged' (zero when not over cap)
Over_Cap_Amount.description: Required when Lifecycle_Stage = 'Charged' (zero when not over cap)
Over_Cap_Amount.synonyms: Over-Cap Salary, NIH Cap Excess, Salary Cap Excess

Activity_Report.definition: An activity report other than a PAR

Certification_Method.description: Constrained when present: PAR / Activity_Report / Timesheet / Other. Required when Lifecycle_Stage = 'Certified'

Certifier_Personnel_ID.synonyms: Effort Certifier, Approving Authority, PAR Certifier

Certification_Statement_Text.conditional_required: Required when Lifecycle_Stage = 'Certified'. Recorded verbatim because the legal force of effort certification depends on what the certifier saw and accepted.
Certification_Statement_Text.description: The legal attestation text the certifier accepted. Required when Lifecycle_Stage = 'Certified'. Recorded verbatim because the legal force of effort certification depends on what the certifier saw and accepted

Certification_Signature_Reference.description: Reference to a stored signature artifact (signed PDF, e-signature service record, IDP claim)

constraints.rule: Effort_Percent is between 0.00 and 100.00.
Charged_Amount and Over_Cap_Amount are required when Lifecycle_Stage = 'Charged'.
Certification_Method, Certifier_Personnel_ID, Certification_Date are required when Lifecycle_Stage = 'Certified'.
When Lifecycle_Stage = 'Certified', all of: Certification_Method, Certifier_Personnel_ID, Certification_Date, Certification_Statement_Text are required.
Person_Months equals Effort_Percent / 100 multiplied by 12 when Calendar_Type = 'Calendar', by 9 when 'Academic', by 3 when 'Summer'.
For a given (TeamRole_ID, Lifecycle_Stage) and active rows only (Is_Active = true), the (Period_Start_Date, Period_End_Date) ranges are non-overlapping.
Effort at Lifecycle_Stage Proposed references a TeamRole row whose Award_ID and Subaward_ID are null; Effort at Approved, Charged, or Certified references a TeamRole row with an agreement.

conventions.name: TeamRole role-bearer changes
conventions.description: When a role-bearer on an Award or Subaward changes (a PI_Change Modification, a coordinator handoff, an off-boarding), the predecessor's TeamRole row is end-dated and a new TeamRole row is inserted for the successor.
rules: The predecessor's End_Date is the day BEFORE the successor's Start_Date (no day-of-transition overlap).
The successor's Start_Date is the first day in role.
TeamRole rows are not mutated in place; the row history is the canonical record of 'who held this role on date D' (Start_Date <= D AND (End_Date IS NULL OR End_Date >= D)).
Because predecessor.End_Date < successor.Start_Date, exactly one row matches a given date and the active-rows sum-to-100 constraint holds across the transition without double-counting.
TeamRole is the canonical source for the PI on an Award; the same insert-and-end-date pattern applies to PI changes.

On award creation every active proposal-stage TeamRole row for the proposal is copied as a new row carrying Award_ID or Subaward_ID and pointing back through Previous_TeamRole_ID; the proposal-stage row is not mutated and remains the record of the proposed team. A role that appears only after funding has no Previous_TeamRole_ID.
conventions.pi_change_modification: A PI_Change Modification documents the sponsor-side approval or notice of a PI change when required. Not required for every PI change; TeamRole row history remains authoritative. When both exist, the Modification's Effective_Date should equal the successor TeamRole's Start_Date.
conventions.nce_extends_open_roles: When an end-date-changing Modification (NCE, etc.) advances Award.Current_End_Date, open TeamRole rows (End_Date null) remain open and are not modified. End-dating happens only at explicit role-bearer changes or at Award_Status closure.

example_views.name: vw_Award_PI_Timeline
example_views.purpose: Full PI history per Award via TeamRole; one row per (Award, Personnel, role-stint). Use the active-on-date predicate at query time to filter to a specific point in time.
example_views.sql:
CREATE VIEW vw_Award_PI_Timeline AS
SELECT
  ar.TeamRole_ID,
  ar.Award_ID,
  ar.Subaward_ID,
  ar.Personnel_ID,
  ar.Start_Date,
  ar.End_Date,
  av.Value_Code AS Role_Code,
  av.Canonical_Value_Code AS Canonical_Role_Code,
  ar.Is_Contact_PI
FROM TeamRole ar
JOIN AllowedValues av ON ar.Role_Value_ID = av.AllowedValue_ID
WHERE av.Canonical_Value_Code IN ('PI', 'Multi_PI')
  AND ar.Is_Active = true;
example_views.usage_example: SELECT Personnel_ID FROM vw_Award_PI_Timeline WHERE Award_ID = :x AND Start_Date <= :date_d AND (End_Date IS NULL OR End_Date >= :date_d);

example_views.name: vw_Effort_Certification_Status
example_views.purpose: Per (Award/Subaward, period) summary of effort rows by Lifecycle_Stage. Highlights periods where Charged effort has not been Certified.
example_views.sql:
CREATE VIEW vw_Effort_Certification_Status AS
SELECT
  ar.Award_ID,
  ar.Subaward_ID,
  e.Period_Start_Date,
  e.Period_End_Date,
  COUNT(*) AS Total_Effort_Rows,
  SUM(CASE WHEN e.Lifecycle_Stage = 'Charged' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS Charged_Count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN e.Lifecycle_Stage = 'Certified' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS Certified_Count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN e.Lifecycle_Stage = 'Charged'
          AND NOT EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM Effort e2
            WHERE e2.Previous_Effort_ID = e.Effort_ID
              AND e2.Lifecycle_Stage = 'Certified'
              AND e2.Is_Active = true)
          THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS Uncertified_Charged_Count
FROM Effort e
JOIN TeamRole ar ON e.TeamRole_ID = ar.TeamRole_ID
WHERE e.Is_Active = true
GROUP BY ar.Award_ID, ar.Subaward_ID, e.Period_Start_Date, e.Period_End_Date;

example_views.name: vw_Active_Personnel_Roles
example_views.purpose: Currently-active TeamRole rows on currently-active Awards or Subawards. Captures the operational 'who is on the team right now' query without per-consumer date filtering.
example_views.sql:
CREATE VIEW vw_Active_Personnel_Roles AS
SELECT
  ar.TeamRole_ID,
  ar.Personnel_ID,
  CONCAT(p.First_Name, ' ', p.Last_Name) AS Personnel_Name,
  ar.Award_ID,
  ar.Subaward_ID,
  COALESCE(a.Award_Number, s.Subaward_Number) AS Agreement_Number,
  rv.Value_Code AS Role_Code,
  rv.Canonical_Value_Code AS Canonical_Role,
  ar.FTE_Percent,
  ar.Credit_Percent,
  ar.Is_Key_Personnel,
  ar.Is_Contact_PI,
  ar.Start_Date,
  ar.End_Date
FROM TeamRole ar
JOIN Personnel p ON ar.Personnel_ID = p.Personnel_ID
LEFT JOIN Award a ON ar.Award_ID = a.Award_ID
LEFT JOIN Subaward s ON ar.Subaward_ID = s.Subaward_ID
JOIN AllowedValues rv ON ar.Role_Value_ID = rv.AllowedValue_ID
WHERE ar.Is_Active = true
  AND ar.Start_Date <= CURRENT_DATE
  AND (ar.End_Date IS NULL OR ar.End_Date >= CURRENT_DATE)
  AND (
    (ar.Award_ID IS NOT NULL AND a.Award_Status = 'Active' AND a.Is_Active = true)
    OR (ar.Subaward_ID IS NOT NULL AND s.Subaward_Status = 'Active' AND s.Is_Active = true)
  );

finance.name: Finance
finance.story: We manage the money: budgets, transactions, rates, payments

Budget.description: Detailed line items for a budget at a specific lifecycle stage. Each Budget row carries Proposal_ID at every stage (stable chain identity) and post-award Award_ID or Subaward_ID at Approved and later stages.

Budget_ID.synonyms: Budget Line, Cost Element, Budget Item

Proposed.definition: The budget as proposed to the sponsor

Approved.definition: The budget as funded in the award

Current.definition: The budget as revised by approved modifications

Actual.definition: What was actually spent for the period

Modular.definition: Modular budget in fixed increments without line items

Previous_Budget_ID.description: Later-stage rows point back to earlier-stage rows (revisions chain)

Proposal_ID.description: Originating Proposal; stable across all Lifecycle_Stages. The Previous_Budget_ID chain spans Proposed -> Approved -> Current -> Actual without changing anchor.

Award_ID.conditional_required: Exactly one of Award_ID or Subaward_ID non-null when Lifecycle_Stage is Approved, Current, or Actual
Award_ID.description: The Award this budget belongs to at post-award stages. Exactly one of Award_ID or Subaward_ID is non-null when Lifecycle_Stage is Approved, Current, or Actual; both null at Proposed.

Subaward_ID.conditional_required: Exactly one of Award_ID or Subaward_ID non-null when Lifecycle_Stage is Approved, Current, or Actual
Subaward_ID.description: The Subaward this budget belongs to at post-award stages. Exactly one of Award_ID or Subaward_ID is non-null when Lifecycle_Stage is Approved, Current, or Actual; both null at Proposed.

Period_Start_Date.description: Start of the budget period this row covers
Period_Start_Date.synonyms: Budget Period Start, Year Start, Budget Year Begin

Period_End_Date.description: End of the budget period this row covers
Period_End_Date.synonyms: Budget Period End, Year End, Budget Year Close

Version_Number.description: Revision number within (Proposal_ID, post-award anchor, Lifecycle_Stage, Period_Start_Date). Starts at 1 in each stage and increments per revision

Module_Size_Amount.conditional_required: Required when Budget_Mode = 'Modular' (typically $25,000 for NIH modular)
Module_Size_Amount.description: Required when Budget_Mode = 'Modular' (typically $25,000 for NIH modular)

Budget_Category_ID.conditional_required: Required when Budget_Mode = 'Itemized'; one Budget row per line item
Budget_Category_ID.description: Required when Budget_Mode = 'Itemized'; one Budget row per line item

Amount.synonyms: Line Amount, Category Amount, Line Item Cost

IndirectRate_ID.description: The F&A (indirect-cost) rate that applies to this Budget period. Set at the Budget granularity because multi-year Awards may use different rates per period. Null when no F&A rate applies.
IndirectRate_ID.synonyms: F&A Rate, Indirect Rate, Overhead Rate, IDC Rate

constraints.rule: Proposal_ID is required at every Lifecycle_Stage; exactly one of Award_ID or Subaward_ID is non-null when Lifecycle_Stage is Approved, Current, or Actual.
Mode-specific required columns: Module_Count and Module_Size_Amount when Budget_Mode = 'Modular'; Budget_Category_ID and Amount when Budget_Mode = 'Itemized'.

At most one row per (Proposal_ID, post-award anchor, Lifecycle_Stage, Period_Start_Date, Version_Number, Budget_Category_ID). For the uniqueness key, null Budget_Category_ID values are treated as a single distinct value.
For a given (Proposal_ID, post-award anchor, Lifecycle_Stage) and active rows only (Is_Active = true), the (Period_Start_Date, Period_End_Date) ranges are non-overlapping.
Outer-edge coverage. For an Award (or Subaward), the MAX Period_End_Date across active Current-stage Budget rows for that anchor equals the Award's Current_End_Date (or Subaward's Current_End_Date).

Inner-edge coverage. For an Award (or Subaward), the MIN Period_Start_Date across active Current-stage Budget rows for that anchor equals the Award's Original_Start_Date (or Subaward's Original_Start_Date).

No gaps between periods. For a given (Proposal_ID, post-award anchor, Lifecycle_Stage) and active rows only, consecutive periods (ordered by Period_Start_Date) have no gap: the next period's Period_Start_Date equals the prior period's Period_End_Date + 1 day.

conventions.name: Modification effect on the Budget chain
conventions.description: A Modification creates a new Current-stage Budget row when it changes any Budget column. The discriminator is which Modification column is non-null, not the event type: Funding_Change_Amount marks a funding change, New_End_Date marks an end-date change. A Modification with both non-null gets both behaviors.

funding_changing.behavior: Change Amount-class columns. New Current row chains via Previous_Budget_ID to the prior Current row (or Approved if no Current exists) for the affected period; Period_End_Date matches the predecessor.

events: typically No_Cost_Extension, Sponsor_Transfer, a Supplement that extends the period
end_date_changing.behavior: Change Period_End_Date on the last existing budget period of the affected anchor. New Current row chains from the prior latest Current row for that last period, Period_End_Date is set to match the new Award.Current_End_Date (or Subaward.Current_End_Date), and amounts stay unchanged.

award_state_only.behavior: Change no Budget column. Do not create a new Budget row; change Award/Subaward state only (TeamRole row history for PI_Change, Award metadata for Scope_Change).

conventions.version_number_rule: Version_Number increments per revision on the same (Proposal_ID, post-award anchor, Period_Start_Date) key for both funding-changing and end-date-changing events.
conventions.chain_identity: Because Budget.Proposal_ID is required at every Lifecycle_Stage, the chain identity is stable across Proposed -> Approved -> Current -> Actual; Award_ID / Subaward_ID is added at Approved+ as the post-award disambiguation anchor without invalidating the Proposal anchor.
conventions.current_stage_immutability: Chain immutability extends to same-stage parenting on Current: once a Current row has a Current descendant via Previous_Budget_ID, the predecessor's amounts and period dates are frozen.
conventions.reversal: When a Modification's Approval_Status becomes Reversed, the Current-stage Budget rows it created are marked Is_Active = false, and the prior Current row for each affected period becomes the active leaf again. No row is edited. The derived Award and Subaward columns already exclude a Reversed Modification, so the chain and the derivations agree.

conventions.name: Budget Proposed-stage revisions
conventions.description: During proposal preparation or in response to a JIT request, a revised Proposed-stage Budget row is inserted chained via Previous_Budget_ID to the prior Proposed row on the same (Proposal_ID, Period_Start_Date) key, with Version_Number incremented.
conventions.transition_to_approved: When the Proposal is awarded and the Approved-stage Budget row is created, its Previous_Budget_ID points at the latest active Proposed row for that period (the one with no Proposed descendant). This is how the Approved-stage row automatically picks up the most recent JIT or proposal-preparation revision without explicit selection logic.

conventions.name: ComplianceCoverage on protocol renewal
conventions.description: When a ComplianceRequirement is renewed (a new ComplianceRequirement row is created with Previous_ComplianceRequirement_ID pointing at the predecessor), the predecessor's open ComplianceCoverage rows are end-dated (Coverage_End_Date set to the renewal date) and new ComplianceCoverage rows are created pointing at the renewed ComplianceRequirement with Coverage_Start_Date equal to the renewal date. Each Award's coverage is thus continuous in queries; the ComplianceRequirement row identity advances on every annual renewal cycle.

conventions.name: Removing one Award from a multi-Award ComplianceCoverage
conventions.description: When a protocol amendment drops coverage of one Award (the requirement still covers the others, no renewal is happening), end-date the specific ComplianceCoverage row only: set Coverage_End_Date to the amendment date and mark Is_Active = false. The ComplianceRequirement and the other Coverage rows are untouched. Distinct from the renewal cascade: renewal advances the ComplianceRequirement row identity and rebuilds the entire Coverage set; amendment-removal touches a single Coverage row.

conventions.name: ConflictOfInterest vs OtherSupport vs ComplianceRequirement(COI)
conventions.description: Three tables touch outside-relationship facts; each answers a different question.

tables.ConflictOfInterest: What did this person disclose to the institution's COI office, and what was the review outcome. Personal disclosure with Relationship_Type (Financial / Consulting / Employment / Equity / Royalty / Board_Membership) and Review_Outcome.
tables.OtherSupport: What active and pending support does this person have on a sponsor biosketch. Sponsor-facing, with Support_Type (Current / Pending / In_Kind) and effort commitment.
tables.ComplianceRequirement with Requirement_T: What is the institutional COI compliance regime under which the disclosures are filed (the annual attestation cycle, the training requirement, the policy artifact).

conventions.link_rule: When ConflictOfInterest and OtherSupport describe the same engagement, the ConflictOfInterest.OtherSupport_ID FK links them. The link is optional; many COI disclosures (royalties, board memberships without active support) have no OtherSupport counterpart.
conventions.foreign_engagement_scope: Foreign-engagement disclosures (foreign affiliations, foreign appointments, foreign talent-program participation, foreign funding sources) are not modeled in the canonical ConflictOfInterest table; institutions subject to NSPM-33 or comparable research-security regimes add a local extension.

conventions.name: Committee membership vs ProtocolRole
conventions.description: Membership on a reviewing committee (the IRB board, the IACUC committee) is an OrganizationRole row on the committee Organization with Role_Value_ID resolving to Member, Chair, etc. Personnel on a submitted protocol (the PI's study team, coordinators, lab manager) are ProtocolRole rows on the ComplianceRequirement. The same person may appear in both contexts.

conventions.name: Recurring compliance renewals
conventions.description: Annual continuing reviews (IRB), annual COI attestations, annual export-control reaffirmations live on the current ComplianceRequirement row itself: Expiration_Date is the date the current approval lapses. When the renewal completes, a new ComplianceRequirement row is created with Previous_ComplianceRequirement_ID pointing at the predecessor.

example_views.name: vw_Active_IRB_Coverage
example_views.purpose: Awards (and Subawards) currently covered by an active IRB ComplianceRequirement. Use the same pattern with WHERE Requirement_Type IN (...) for other regimes.
example_views.sql:
CREATE VIEW vw_Active_IRB_Coverage AS
SELECT
  cv.ComplianceCoverage_ID,
  cv.Award_ID,
  cv.Subaward_ID,
  cr.ComplianceRequirement_ID,
  cr.Compliance_Number,
  cr.Approved_Date,
  cr.Expiration_Date,
  cv.Coverage_Start_Date
FROM ComplianceCoverage cv
JOIN ComplianceRequirement cr ON cv.ComplianceRequirement_ID = cr.ComplianceRequirement_ID
WHERE cr.Requirement_Type = 'IRB'
  AND cr.Requirement_Status = 'Approved'
  AND (cr.Expiration_Date IS NULL OR cr.Expiration_Date >= CURRENT_DATE)
  AND cv.Coverage_End_Date IS NULL
  AND cv.Is_Active = true
  AND cr.Is_Active = true;

Returned_for_Revision.definition: Sent back for changes; the step is rerun in the next round

constraints.rule: Approver_Personnel_ID and Action_Date are required when Approval_Status is Approved, Rejected, Bypassed, or Returned_for_Revision.
Review_Topic_Value_ID is required when Step_Type resolves to Supplementary_Review.
Signed_Package_Hash is required when Step_Type resolves to Final_Sign_off and Approval_Status is Approved.
Delegate_Personnel_ID is required when Step_Type resolves to Release_to_Submit and Approval_Status is Approved.
Blocks: within one (Related_Entity_Type, Related_Entity_ID, Approval_Round), no row leaves Pending while a row with a lower Approval_Step_Order is Pending.
Rounds: a step that is Returned_for_Revision is not reopened; the rerun steps are new rows with Approval_Round one higher. Approval_Round is consecutive from 1 within the record.

Voiding: a Final_Sign_off row whose Signed_Package_Hash no longer equals the hash of the record's current package becomes Voided, and any Release_to_Submit row that followed it in the same round becomes Voided with it.
Related_Entity_ID references an existing row in the table named by Related_Entity_Type (polymorphic attachment enforcement).

conventions.name: Deadline vs first-class due dates
conventions.description: Several entities carry their own due-date columns (Report.Due_Date, Closeout milestones, RFA.Submission_Deadline, RFA.LOI_Deadline, ComplianceRequirement.Expiration_Date). The Deadline attachment is for ad-hoc obligations that don't have a first-class entity. Use Deadline only for obligations that don't otherwise have a structured home.

conventions.name: Attachments vs row properties
conventions.description: Restriction and Classification are modeled as polymorphic attachments because they recur across many parent types. Treat them as first-class records that happen to attach polymorphically rather than as system metadata.

conventions.name: Action.Outcome_Description
conventions.description: When an Action records a structured workflow with a substantive result (Subrecipient_Risk_Review, Modification_Approval, Cost_Transfer_Approval), the outcome lives in Outcome_Description plus an optional Linked_Document_ID for the formal report.

conventions.name: Approval chains
conventions.description: How a record is routed for approval, on any record type Approval attaches to.
rules: Each step names what is decided (Step_Type) and who decides it (Approval_Role). An institution's chain is a row template the application applies at routing time; the order of blocks is institutional configuration, not the standard's.

A Department_Review is one row per department represented on the team, a College_Review one per college; Reviewing_Organization_ID names the unit. A Supplementary_Review is one row per topic that applies.
Rows sharing Approval_Step_Order form a block and run in parallel. A block waits on the previous one.
A return does not reopen rows: the rerun steps are new rows in the next Approval_Round.

Final_Sign_off is the authorized organizational representative's approval of an assembled package and records its hash. Release_to_Submit releases the signed package to a named person. Any change to the package voids both. Transmitting the package is a SubmissionAttempt, not an approval.

Internal routing of a Modification request is Approval rows on the Modification; Modification.Approval_Status remains the sponsor's decision. Automated pre-submission checks are not approvals and do not get rows.

example_views.name: vw_Active_Restrictions
example_views.purpose: Currently-in-force Restriction rows across all attachable entity types, with the Restriction_Type resolved.
example_views.sql:
CREATE VIEW vw_Active_Restrictions AS
SELECT
  r.Restriction_ID,
  r.Related_Entity_Type,
  r.Related_Entity_ID,
  rt.Value_Code AS Restriction_Type_Code,
  rt.Canonical_Value_Code AS Canonical_Restriction_Type,
  r.Restriction_Level,
  r.Effective_Start_Date,
  r.Effective_End_Date,
  r.Restriction_Status
FROM Restriction r
JOIN AllowedValues rt ON r.Restriction_Type_Value_ID = rt.AllowedValue_ID
WHERE r.Restriction_Status = 'Active'
  AND r.Effective_Start_Date <= CURRENT_DATE
  AND (r.Effective_End_Date IS NULL OR r.Effective_End_Date >= CURRENT_DATE)
  AND r.Is_Active = true;

compliance_protocols.name: Compliance Protocols
compliance_protocols.notes: The shared protocol spine. One Protocol carries exactly one Regime and one reviewing authority; multi-regime work is multiple Protocols covering the same funding instruments. The four event entities (Amendment, ContinuingReview, AdverseEvent, Deviation) have their own approval lifecycles and are all reviewed via the shared polymorphic ProtocolReviewStep. Notification cycles (e.g. designated-member-review polling) compose from core Communication + Deadline + CommunicationResponse attached to the Protocol; this module adds no notification entities. With this module adopted, protocol rosters live in ProtocolPersonnel; the core ProtocolRole remains for requirement-scoped staffing where the module is not in play.

governance.name: Governance
